answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a work bond earned only through verified, costly computation and peer-attested service, rather than mere registration. Like a ridge that shelters a valley from a gale, this bond raises the cost of spawning hollow identities: creating a thousand fake agents would require a thousand bonds, each locked and slashed if the agent misbehaves. Honest agents recover their bond over time through useful work, while attackers lose capital faster than they can profit, making large-scale fakery economically irrational.
